ref_text.narrator: This temple was not built, it was carved from a single rock. Twelve hundred years ago, workers cut straight down into a mountain.

jobs.text: They say this temple's shadow never touches the ground.
That's a myth. But the truth is even crazier.
This is the Brihadeeswarar Temple, in Thanjavoor, Tamil Nadu.
King Raja Raja Chola built it around the year ten-ten. More than a thousand years ago.
Its tower rises about sixty-six metres. Like a twenty-storey building.
It is made of around one hundred and thirty thousand tonnes of granite.
But Thanjavoor is flat river land. There are no granite hills nearby.
Every block was hauled in from far away.
And the top stone? It is said to weigh about eighty tonnes.
No cranes. So how did it get sixty-six metres up?
Legend says they built a ramp, about six kilometres long.
Elephants and people dragged it up... inch by inch.
Even the Nandi at the entrance is carved from one single rock.
And the shadow? It does fall on the ground.
At noon, it simply hides under the temple's own base.
A thousand years later, it still stands. A UNESCO World Heritage Site.
